context.process_name: Two-Ledger Allocation Framework (Capital vs Carry Interest)
context.objective: Document how we carry out Two-Ledger Allocation Framework (Capital vs Carry Interest), the controls and what needs confirmation.

turns.text: It is less a single trigger and more a framework we apply whenever GP vehicle economics have to be split among members. That happens on each periodic allocation, on each capital call or distribution event, or when there is an approved change to the member population that affects GP economics. The core idea is that every member has two separate interests: a capital interest, which is allocated on approved commitment or contribution information, and a carry interest, which allocates the approved vehicle-level carry amount under approved carry schedules. We keep those in two separate ledgers and only combine them by member at the end, because a percentage from one ledger can never stand in for the percentage in the other. Before any calculating we need the approved event total or the amount passed down from the upstream process in hand. There is no contractual deadline or cutoff established for it.
Talk me through how you keep the capital and carry ledgers separate and allocate each one for an event.

Conceptually, a few rules govern it. Governing documents outrank client elections, internal practice, systems, workbooks and what people remember; if they conflict, processing stops until the right authority resolves it. The capital ledger uses only the client-approved method, which is either whole-population, deal, or tranche, and for a realized event we use only the approved contributions tied to that event, deal or tranche. The carry ledger is always life-to-date: we calculate carry from inception through the current period under each applicable schedule and subtract all carry recorded in prior periods, and the remainder is the current-period entry. Calculating only the current period is not acceptable. The two ledgers sit in separate sections of an Excel allocation workbook and are combined by member only after each is done. Any reallocation between members has to net to zero in each affected ledger, and a member's reduction can only go to recipients the client names. Members can validly move in opposite directions, so we explain those results rather than force them to look uniform. I, as the GPFS Preparer, calculate both ledgers and a GPFS Reviewer independently recalculates.
When the independent recalculation does not match, what happens before the allocation can proceed?

Every unexplained difference has to be investigated and resolved, because no tolerance for a difference has ever been approved, so we require exact reconciliation and no shortcuts. What we do depends on where the mismatch is. On the capital side, if contributions, event population and allocated totals do not agree, and the cause is missing or unreliable deal or tranche tags or mapping, we stop work on that component and get corrected data or an approved mapping from the client or source provider; we do not infer it, and we do not record the entry or publish. On the carry side, if life-to-date carry minus prior recorded carry does not give the current-period entry, we stop and reconcile. If capital plus carry does not equal the combined member schedule and the approved event total, we investigate and do not force the result. The Reviewer stops release if a difference is unexplained, the basis is unsupported, or records are incomplete. Who formally approves and releases is not confirmed, I do not know that.
What can happen if an allocation is released with an unexplained error?

GP economics could be created or lost if a reallocation does not net to zero, the current-period carry entry could be wrong, or the published allocation might not match the approved result. That matters because the event allocation feeds the GP workbook and the capital call or distribution process before notices go out or cash moves. Unusual results might also not be reproducible later. How to correct something already released is not defined, I do not know that. Since order matters here, the sequence is seven steps. One, I confirm the event and governing basis, set up separate capital and carry sections, and record the source period and purpose, which starts the event workpaper. Two, I reconcile member and schedule changes, confirm effective dates and components covered, and freeze the dated approved versions, with the client confirming; that gives a locked input set. Three, I calculate the capital-interest ledger. Four, I calculate the carry-interest ledger, giving the carry rollforward and current-period entry. Five, I combine results by member, reconcile to the event total and explain members moving in different directions, with the Reviewer involved and the client confirming when the intended result is unclear. Six, if there is an approved reallocation, I apply equal and opposite member changes and prove net zero per affected ledger, with the client naming recipients. Seven, the Reviewer completes the independent review, the approved version is locked, it is used to update the GP workbook or the downstream capital call or distribution file, the output is reconciled to the locked package, and the records are kept.
What upstream process provides the approved event total, and how do you know it is ready to use?

The event total comes from the approved source event file, or as a handoff from the waterfall and clawback process, which gives the approved vehicle-level carry or holdback result, or from the quarterly GP workbook process. It is ready when it is final and approved and I have confirmed it matches the correct event and period. Two other upstream feeds matter too: the member changes process gives approved member changes before the affected capital allocation, and the carry vesting process gives approved points and effective schedules before the affected carry allocation. On the exception paths: if the governing basis is absent, ambiguous or conflicts with a client instruction, I record the conflict and get a current interpretation from the governing authority, an adviser or the client, and calculation, entry and release stay blocked until there is a written resolution, then we continue from confirming the basis. If a carry schedule is missing, overlapping, conflicting or out of date, the affected carry calculation stops, the client supplies a corrected approved schedule set, and we recalculate carry and all affected downstream outputs. If a source, schedule, population or output changes after work starts or after review, every affected calculation and reconciliation is repeated and any unreleased output is stopped; who decides on correction or reissue is not confirmed, I do not know. The work is finished when the final output agrees with the locked reviewed package at total and member level and the handoff is done.
Does this framework have another name used by your team or in a checklist or system?

memo_findings.answer: Two-Ledger Allocation Framework (Capital vs Carry Interest)
The framework splits GP vehicle economics among members using separate capital and carry interests.

The framework is applied on each periodic allocation, each capital call or distribution event, and when an approved change to the member population affects GP economics. Before calculating, the approved event total or amount passed down from an upstream process must be in hand; no contractual deadline or cutoff is established.

The two completed ledgers are combined by member at the end of the calculation.
Exact reconciliation is required, and the Reviewer stops release for unexplained differences, an unsupported basis or incomplete records. For a capital mismatch caused by missing or unreliable tags or mapping, the entry is not recorded or published while the component is stopped.
Completion includes independent review, locking the approved version, updating the GP workbook or downstream capital call or distribution file, reconciling output to the locked package, and keeping records.
The work is finished when the final output agrees with the locked reviewed package at total and member level and the handoff is done.

For an allocation, call, distribution, or approved member-population change affecting GP economics, the framework keeps capital and carry interests in separate ledgers and combines them by member only at the end.
The GPFS Preparer calculates both ledgers in separate sections of an Excel allocation workbook; the GPFS Reviewer independently recalculates. The ledgers are combined by member only after each is done.
For a realized event, the capital ledger uses approved contributions tied to that event, deal or tranche. Carry is calculated from inception through the current period under each applicable schedule, less all carry recorded in prior periods, to determine the current-period entry.
If governing documents conflict with lower-ranking sources, processing stops until the right authority resolves the conflict. Opposite member movements are explained rather than forced to look uniform.
If a capital mismatch is caused by missing or unreliable deal or tranche tags or mapping, work stops on that component until corrected data or an approved mapping is obtained from the client or source provider. The mapping is not inferred, and the entry is not recorded or published.
If life-to-date carry less prior recorded carry does not equal the current-period entry, work stops and the carry is reconciled. If capital plus carry does not equal the combined member schedule and approved event total, the difference is investigated rather than forced.
The GPFS Preparer confirms the event and governing basis, sets up separate capital and carry sections, and records the source period and purpose to start the event workpaper.
The Preparer reconciles member and schedule changes, confirms effective dates and covered components, and freezes dated approved versions with client confirmation to produce a locked input set.
The Preparer calculates capital first, then carry, producing the carry rollforward and current-period entry. The Preparer combines results by member, reconciles them to the event total and explains opposite movements, with Reviewer involvement and client confirmation when the intended result is unclear.
If a reallocation is approved, the Preparer applies equal and opposite member changes and proves net zero in each affected ledger; the client names recipients.
The Reviewer completes independent review, the approved version is locked, and it is used to update the GP workbook or downstream capital call or distribution file. The output is reconciled to the locked package and records are retained.
